anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet (mcu.kicad_sch, tile 1/4) the global net label 'HEATER' is attached to U1 pin 13 (GPIO1), to U6 pins 1 and 2 (DIAG_EN and IN), and to J5 pin 2 and the D2/R3 indicator branch. The actual switched heater output, U6 pin 7 (OUT), is wired only to J5's sibling connector J6 pin 2 and carries no 'HEATER' label. So the status LED D2 + R3 and an extra screw terminal J5 sit on the GPIO1 control net, while the power-switched output net is unlabeled.

A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the HEATER net, so the heater output doubles as a visual heater on indicator', while the drive signal is the hierarchical net '/Microcontroller/HEATER' on 'IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) ... driven from ESP32 GPIO1'. D2/R3 must therefore be on the U6 OUT net, and there must be no screw terminal (J5) tying the GPIO1 control net to GND.

anomalies.impact: The 'heater on' LED now follows the 3.3 V GPIO1 command instead of the 12 V switched output, so it can light even when U6 is open, the element is disconnected, or the output is shorted, giving a false heater-on indication; and the extra terminal J5 provides a user-accessible path that shorts the MCU control pin to GND when mated.
